title: RSS Reader
summary: A text-feed reader for the deck: pin your favorite news, tech and science feeds from a catalog of about 260 by country and topic, or add any site by its address, then read the articles full screen, by touch or keyboard, on any screen from 640x480 up.
description: A full-screen reader of RSS and Atom feeds (text feeds only: no podcasts or video). It opens on a Home list (Favorites with the count of new articles, Browse feeds, Saved articles, Add a feed, Settings); each page has a header with an Esc button. Browse feeds walks a bundled catalog of about 260 hand-checked feeds by country (or International), then topic, then feed, each with its language and whether it carries the full text or a summary; a search finds a feed by name, site or topic across the whole catalog, and a tap on a selected feed pins it to your favorites (a blue dot) or unpins it. Add a feed takes a site's address (example.com) or a feed's: the feed is found for you, then you pin it. Favorites lists your feeds in your order with their unread counts and the age of their newest article; Refresh all updates them one after the other in the background (only what changed is downloaded), and they can be updated each time you open the page. A feed's articles show unread ones with a blue dot; opening one shows its title, source, date, text (headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes) and pictures (JPEG, PNG, GIF and BMP, downloaded in the background and kept in a 50 MB cache; a tap shows one full screen) in the text size you choose, Left and Right go to the previous and next article. Save for offline keeps an article with its pictures, readable without the network, under a storage cap you choose. The options of a feed (move, unpin, mark all read, refresh, details) or of an article (read or unread, save for offline, article info, text size) open with a 3 s hold on its row or on the text, or Ctrl+O. Settings: text size, refresh when opening, the storage cap for saved articles, clear the read history, export and import your favorites as an OPML file in your home folder. Only the feeds themselves are fetched (with curl), never the web pages behind them; nothing is sent anywhere else. Favorites, read marks and settings are kept in ~/.local/share/rss-reader. Text is typed with a Bluetooth or USB keyboard, or with the launcher's on-screen keyboard while none is connected. Needs the network to update the feeds (what was fetched stays readable offline), a screen of at least 640x480 and a launcher with full-screen app support (X-Fullscreen in .desktop files).
